dialogue.text: Woof! (The professor's dog eyes you like a reviewer.)
Woof woof. (Andreas is in his office. Bring a proof, not an excuse.)
The dog approves. Your thesis feels 10% more sound.
The dog sighs. Somewhere, a loop fails to terminate.
Hi! I'm Byron. Visiting from Cambridge.
Andreas and I have been arguing about termination proofs for years. He's usually right.
Keep going with the verification stuff. One day we'll run it on the whole cloud.
Martin! I'm stuck on these GUI tests again.
What if we translate Java bytecode into Boogie and just look for code that can never run?
We could call it... Joogie. No? Fine, I'll think of something better. (He won't.)
Hey Martin. I've been thinking about error traces.
What if we could compute which parts of a failing trace actually matter? Error invariants!
Grab the papers lying around campus. Your thesis isn't going to write itself.
Martin! I read your paper on doomed program points.
We do similar work at UNU-IIST in Macau. Come visit. The exit is that way.
